source_text: Οὐ μὴν οὐδὲ ἀὴρ προκάλυμμα ἦν τότε τῆς γῆς. Ἀραιὰ γὰρ καὶ διαφανὴς τοῦ ἀέρος ἡ φύσις, πάντα τὰ εἴδη τῶν ὁρατῶν δεχομένη, καὶ ταῖς τῶν ὁρώντων ὄψεσι παραπέμπουσα. Λειπόμενον τοίνυν ἐστὶ νοεῖν ἡμᾶς ὕδωρ ἐπιπολάζειν τῇ ἐπιφανείᾳ τῆς γῆς, οὔπω πρὸς τὴν οἰκείαν λῆξιν τῆς ὑγρᾶς οὐσίας ἀποκριθείσης. Ἐκ δὲ τούτου οὐ μόνον ἀόρατος ἦν ἡ γῆ, ἀλλὰ καὶ ἀκατασκεύαστος. Ἡ γὰρ τοῦ ὑγροῦ πλεονεξία ἔτι καὶ νῦν ἐμπόδιόν ἐστι πρὸς καρπογονίαν τῇ γῇ. Ἡ οὖν αὐτὴ αἰτία, καὶ τοῦ μὴ ὁρᾶσθαι, καὶ τοῦ ἀκατασκεύαστον εἶναι· εἴπερ κατασκευὴ γῆς, ὁ οἰκεῖος αὐτῇ καὶ κατὰ φύσιν κόσμος, λήϊα μὲν ταῖς κοιλότησιν ἐγκυμαίνοντα, λειμῶνες χλοάζοντες καὶ ποικίλοις ἄνθεσι βρύοντες, νάπαι εὐθαλεῖς, καὶ ὀρῶν κορυφαὶ ταῖς ὕλαις κατάσκιοι· ὧν οὐδὲν εἶχεν οὐδέπω· ὠδίνουσα μὲν τὴν πάντων γένεσιν διὰ τὴν ἐναποτεθεῖσαν αὐτῇ παρὰ τοῦ δημιουργοῦ δύναμιν, ἀναμένουσα δὲ τοὺς καθήκοντας χρόνους, ἵνα τῷ θείῳ κελεύσματι προαγάγῃ ἑαυτῆς εἰς φανερὸν τὰ κυήματα. 2.4 Ἀλλὰ καὶ σκότος, φησὶν, ἐπάνω τῆς ἀβύσσου· Πάλιν ἄλλαι μύθων ἀφορμαὶ, καὶ πλασμάτων δυσσεβεστέρων ἀρχαὶ πρὸς τὰς ἰδίας ὑπονοίας παρατρεπόντων τὰ ῥήματα. Τὸ γὰρ σκότος οὐχ ὡς πέφυκεν ἐξηγοῦνται ἀέρα τινὰ ἀφώτιστον, ἢ τόπον ἐξ ἀντιφράξεως σώματος σκιαζόμενον, ἢ ὅλως καθ' ὁποιανοῦν αἰτίαν τόπον φωτὸς ἐστερημένον, ἀλλὰ δύναμιν κακὴν, μᾶλλον δὲ αὐτὸ τὸ κακὸν, παρ' ἑαυτοῦ τὴν ἀρχὴν ἔχον, ἀντικείμενον καὶ ἐναντίον τῇ ἀγαθότητι τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐξηγοῦνται τὸ σκότος. Εἰ γὰρ ὁ Θεὸς φῶς ἐστι, δηλονότι ἡ ἀντιστρατευομένη αὐτῷ δύναμις σκότος ἂν εἴη, φησὶ, κατὰ τὸ τῆς διανοίας ἀκόλουθον. Σκότος, οὐ παρ' ἑτέρου τὸ εἶναι ἔχον, ἀλλὰ κακὸν αὐτογέννητον. Σκότος, πολέμιον ψυχῶν, θανάτου ποιητικὸν, ἀρετῆς ἐναντίωσις· ὅπερ καὶ ὑφεστάναι, καὶ μὴ παρὰ Θεοῦ γεγενῆσθαι, ὑπ' αὐτῶν μηνύεσθαι τῶν τοῦ προφήτου λόγων ἐξαπατῶνται. Ἐκ δὴ τούτου τί οὐχὶ συνεπλάσθη τῶν πονηρῶν καὶ ἀθέων δογμάτων; Ποῖοι λύκοι βαρεῖς διασπῶντες τὸ ποίμνιον τοῦ Θεοῦ, οὐχὶ ἀπὸ τῆς μικρᾶς ταύτης φωνῆς τὴν ἀρχὴν λαβόντες ἐπεπόλασαν ταῖς ψυχαῖς; Οὐχὶ Μαρκιῶνες; οὐχὶ Οὐαλεντῖνοι ἐντεῦθεν; οὐχ ἡ βδελυκτὴ τῶν Μανιχαίων αἵρεσις, ἣν σηπεδόνα τις τῶν Ἐκκλησιῶν προσειπὼν οὐχ ἁμαρτήσεται τοῦ προσήκοντος; Τί μακρὰν ἀποτρέχεις τῆς ἀληθείας, ἄνθρωπε, ἀφορμὰς σεαυτῷ τῆς ἀπωλείας ἐπι νοῶν; Ἁπλοῦς ὁ λόγος, καὶ πᾶσιν εὔληπτος. Ἀόρατος ἦν ἡ γῆ, φησί. Τίς ἡ αἰτία; Ἐπειδὴ ἄβυσσον εἶχεν ἐπιπολάζουσαν ἑαυτῇ. Ἀβύσσου δὲ ἔννοια τίς; Ὕδωρ πολὺ δυσέφικτον ἔχον ἑαυτοῦ τὸ πέρας ἐπὶ τὸ κάτω. Ἀλλ' ἔγνωμεν πολλὰ τῶν σωμάτων καὶ δι' ὕδατος λεπτοτέρου καὶ διαυγοῦς πολλάκις διαφαινόμενα. Πῶς οὖν οὐδὲν μέρος τῆς γῆς διὰ τῶν ὑδάτων ἐδείκνυτο; Ὅτι ἀλαμπὴς ἔτι καὶ ἐσκοτισμένος ἦν ὁ ὑπὲρ αὐτοῦ κεχυμένος ἀήρ. Ἀκτὶς μὲν γὰρ ἡλίου δι' ὑδάτων διικνουμένη, δείκνυσι πολλάκις τὰς ἐν τῷ βάθει ψηφῖδας· ἐν νυκτὶ δέ τις βαθείᾳ οὐδενὶ ἂν τρόπῳ τὰ ὑπὸ τὸ ὕδωρ κατίδοι. Ὥστε τοῦ ἀόρατον εἶναι τὴν γῆν κατασκευαστικόν ἐστι τὸ ἐπαγόμενον, ὅτι καὶ ἄβυσσος ἦν ἡ ἐπέχουσα, καὶ αὕτη ἐσκοτισμένη. Οὔτε οὖν ἄβυσσος, δυνάμεων πλῆθος ἀντικειμένων, ὥς τινες ἐφαντάσθησαν· οὔτε σκότος, ἀρχική τις καὶ πονηρὰ δύναμις ἀντεξαγομένη τῷ ἀγαθῷ.
thought_title: Water and darkness explained literally, against heretical myths
orientation: Basil is explaining why Genesis says the earth was invisible and unformed, arguing that water covered it and the air above was dark, and he begins refuting those who make darkness an evil power.
pass_a_gloss: Nor indeed was air a covering then of the earth. For thin and transparent is the nature of air, receiving all the forms of visible things, and passing them along to the eyes of those who see. It remains therefore for us to understand that water was spread over the surface of the earth, the wet substance not yet having been separated off to its own place. And from this not only was the earth invisible, but also unformed. For the excess of moisture even now is a hindrance to fruit-bearing for the earth. The same cause, then, both of its not being seen and of its being unformed; since the furnishing of the earth is the order proper to it and according to nature: grain-fields swelling in the hollows, meadows growing green and bursting with varied flowers, glens flourishing, and mountain peaks shaded by woods; of which it had none as yet; travailing with the birth of all things because of the power deposited in it by the creator, but awaiting the fitting times, so that at the divine command it might bring forth its offspring into the open. But also darkness, it says, was over the deep. Again other starting points for myths, and beginnings of more impious fabrications, for those who twist the words to their own suspicions. For they do not interpret darkness as it is by nature—some unlit air, or a place shadowed by the blocking of a body, or in general by whatever cause a place deprived of light—but they interpret darkness as an evil power, or rather evil itself, having its beginning from itself, opposed and contrary to the goodness of God. For if God is light, clearly the power arrayed against him would be darkness, it says, according to the consequence of the thought. Darkness, not having its being from another, but evil self-begotten. Darkness, enemy of souls, productive of death, opposition to virtue; which both exists and was not made by God—they are deceived, as they claim, by the very words of the prophet. From this, then, what was not fabricated of wicked and godless doctrines? What heavy wolves tearing apart the flock of God, having taken their start from this small phrase, did not surface upon the souls? Not the Marcionites? Not the Valentinians from here? Not the abominable heresy of the Manichaeans, which someone calling a gangrene of the Churches will not miss what is fitting? Why do you run far from the truth, O man, devising for yourself starting points of destruction? The word is simple and easy for all to grasp. The earth was invisible, it says. What is the cause? Because it had the deep spread over it. And what is the thought of the deep? Much water having its limit hard to reach downward. But we know that many bodies often appear through water that is thinner and clear. How then was no part of the earth shown through the waters? Because the air poured over it was still without light and darkened. For a ray of the sun passing through waters often shows the pebbles in the depth; but in deep night no one in any way could see the things under the water. So that for the earth's being invisible, what is brought in is constructive: that the deep was what covered it, and this was darkened. Neither therefore is the deep a multitude of opposing powers, as some imagined; nor is darkness some ruling and wicked power arrayed against the good.

lemmas.gloss: to be spread over, float on the surface

choices.why: The glossary gives 'invisible and unformed' for the pair; here the single adjective is rendered consistently with that fixed term.
The glossary requires 'the deep' for this term, not 'abyss' or 'watery depths'.
The glossary requires 'darkness' for this term, not 'gloom' or 'shadow'.
Renders the noun from the same root as ἀκατασκεύαστος, keeping the wordplay visible in English.
The medical term 'gangrene' conveys the destructive, spreading corruption Basil attributes to the Manichaean heresy.
Captures the military sense of a force drawn up in opposition to the good.

pass_b_english: Nor was air the covering of the earth at that time. The nature of air is thin and transparent: it receives every form of visible things and passes them on to the eyes of those who see. What remains, then, is for us to understand that water lay spread over the surface of the earth, since the moist substance had not yet been separated off to its own proper place. And for this reason the earth was not only invisible but also unformed. For even now an excess of moisture hinders the earth from bearing fruit. The same cause, then, accounts both for its not being seen and for its being unformed—if indeed the furnishing of the earth is the order proper to it and according to nature: grain fields swelling in the hollows, meadows green and bursting with varied flowers, fertile glens, and mountain peaks shaded by forests. None of these it yet possessed. It was in labor with the birth of all things through the power placed in it by the Creator, but it was waiting for the appointed times, so that at the divine command it might bring forth its offspring into the open.

But “darkness,” it says, “was over the deep” (Genesis 1:2). Here again are other starting points for myths and beginnings of more impious fabrications, for those who twist the words to their own private notions. They do not explain darkness as it actually is—air without light, or a place shadowed by the blocking of a body, or in general a place deprived of light for whatever reason—but they explain darkness as an evil power, or rather evil itself, having its origin from itself, opposed and contrary to the goodness of God. For if God is light, they say, then clearly the power arrayed against him would be darkness, according to the logic of their thought. Darkness, they say, that does not have its being from another, but is a self-begotten evil. Darkness, an enemy of souls, a maker of death, the opposite of virtue. And they are deceived into thinking that this darkness both exists and was not made by God, on the basis of the very words of the prophet. From this, what wicked and godless doctrines have not been fabricated? What heavy wolves, tearing apart the flock of God, have not taken their start from this little phrase and spread over souls? Were not the Marcionites from here? Were not the Valentinians from here? Was not the abominable heresy of the Manichaeans from here—which one would not be wrong to call a gangrene of the churches? Why do you run so far from the truth, O man, devising for yourself starting points of destruction? The word is simple and easy for all to grasp. The earth was invisible, it says. What is the cause? Because it had the deep spread over it. And what is the meaning of “the deep”? Much water, hard to reach, whose limit is downward. But we know that many bodies often appear through water that is thinner and clear. How then was no part of the earth shown through the waters? Because the air poured over it was still without light and darkened. A ray of the sun passing through waters often shows the pebbles in the depths; but in deep night no one could in any way see what is under the water. So the statement that follows confirms that the earth was invisible: because the deep was what covered it, and this deep was darkened. Therefore the deep is not a multitude of opposing powers, as some have imagined; nor is darkness an original and evil power arrayed against the good.

last_rejected.quote: the deep was what covered it, and this deep was darkened
last_rejected.source_quote: ὅτι καὶ ἄβυσσος ἦν ἡ ἐπέχουσα, καὶ αὕτη ἐσκοτισμένη
last_rejected.why: English says 'this deep was darkened' but Greek says 'and this [air] was darkened'—αὕτη refers back to the darkened air, not the deep.
last_rejected.fix: because the deep was what covered it, and this [air] was darkened.
last_rejected.ruling: αὕτη grammatically agrees with ἄβυσσος (fem.); context supports 'this deep' as darkened.

last_rejected.why: ἐναντίωσις means 'opposition/hostility to virtue' or 'adversary of virtue,' not 'the opposite of virtue' as a metaphysical counterpart.
last_rejected.fix: hostile to virtue, or an adversary of virtue
last_rejected.ruling: ἐναντίωσις means 'opposition/contrary'; 'opposite of virtue' is within normal semantic range.

last_rejected.why: αὐτογέννητον means 'self-generated/self-produced,' not 'self-begotten' (which implies begetting/offspring); the point is auto-generation, not auto-begottenness.
last_rejected.ruling: αὐτογέννητον = self-begotten/self-generated; 'self-begotten' is standard rendering, not a major error.

last_rejected.quote: they say, then clearly the power arrayed against him would be darkness
last_rejected.source_quote: φησὶ, κατὰ τὸ τῆς διανοίας ἀκόλουθον
last_rejected.why: The φησὶ marks the opponents' words continuing ('they say'), but English 'they say' is placed only after 'darkness,' making 'then clearly...' sound like Basil's own reasoning rather than the opponents'.
last_rejected.fix: they say, then clearly, according to the logic of their thought, the power arrayed against him would be darkness
last_rejected.ruling: English 'they say' before the quoted claim marks all following as opponents' view; placement is acceptable.
